podcast.body: Released in 1995, this album was intended as a concept album exploring southern identity, specifically "white southern southern identity," possibly as an attempt to create a record similar to Bruce Springsteen's work. However, it is generally considered an inferior record and reflective of the "Lost Cause" theory, a post-Civil War narrative that sought to honor Confederate soldiers and their cause, but failed to condemn slavery. "What he made is what is considered to be a not a great record in B an album that is reflective of the lost cause that's the post civil war theory that told us that the Confederate cause and those who fought for it were honorable that you would not you can you can honor those who fought for a cause that was bigger than themselves you can do that."
